extracted.intended_audience: parties, applicants, licensees, commenters, and counsel participating in FCC proceedings and filings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory procedural rules governing practice before the Federal Communications Commission, including initiation of proceedings, declaratory rulings, waivers, and detailed rules for computing filing and response times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings before the Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may on its own motion or petition of any interested party hold such proceedings as it may deem necessary ... For such purposes it may subpena witnesses and require the production of evidence. Procedures to be followed by the Commission shall, unless specifically prescribed in this part, be such as in the opinion of the Commission will best serve the purposes of such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes that the Commission may initiate or entertain proceedings to investigate matters within its authority and may use compulsory process; procedural choices are governed by what the Commission considers will best serve the purposes of the proceedings unless specific rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory rulings procedure and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may ... issue a declaratory ruling terminating a controversy or removing uncertainty. The bureau or office to which a petition for declaratory ruling has been submitted or assigned ... should docket such a petition within an existing or current proceeding ... and seek comment on the petition via public notice. Unless otherwise specified ... the filing deadline for responsive pleadings to a docketed petition for declaratory ruling will be 30 days from the release date of the public notice, and the default filing deadline for any replies will be 15 days thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect docketing within an existing proceeding if issues substantially relate; bureaus will seek comments by public notice and typical default deadlines are 30 days for responses and 15 days for replies unless the bureau specifies otherwise. See cited Federal Register cross-reference for prior practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension, amendment, or waiver of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this chapter may be suspended, revoked, amended, or waived for good cause shown, in whole or in part, at any time by the Commission, subject to the Administrative Procedure Act and the provisions of this chapter. Any provision of the rules may be waived by the Commission on its own motion or on petition if good cause therefor is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to waive or amend rules require demonstration of good cause; the Commission also has authority to act sua sponte, but must comply with APA constraints and any controlling provisions in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of §1.4 (computation of time)
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule section details the method for computing the amount of time within which persons or entities must act in response to deadlines established by the Commission. It also applies to computation of time for seeking both reconsideration and judicial review of Commission decisions, and prescribes the method for computing the amount of time within which the Commission must act in response to deadlines established by statute, a Commission rule, or Commission order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use §1.4 as the primary framework for all timing computations unless a specific provision states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule when action is initiated by Commission or staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided, the first day to be counted when a period of time begins with an action taken by the Commission, an Administrative Law Judge or by members of the Commission or its staff pursuant to delegated authority is the day after the day on which public notice of that action is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All rules measuring time from a 'Public Notice' are calculated in accordance with this provision; see specific categories of what constitutes 'public notice' in paragraph (b). Examples (1–7) illustrate Federal Register publication, release dates, Public Notice documents, and dates appearing on mailed documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of public notice (types of events that start time computations)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of §1.4, 'public notice' means the date of any of the following events: (1) publication in the Federal Register for documents required to be published there; (2) release date for non-rulemaking documents; (3) Federal Register publication date for rulemakings of particular applicability if Commission so states, otherwise release date; (4) release date of a descriptive 'Public Notice' when full text is not released; (5) the date appearing on a document sent to persons affected where neither publication nor release occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph enumerates the alternative triggering events for public notice; numerous examples (1–7) accompany these subparagraphs to show how to compute the first day in varying scenarios (e.g., FR publication vs. release date vs. mailed documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule when action is initiated by act, event, or default
rubrics_metrics.description: When a period begins with the occurrence of an act, event or default and terminates a specific number of days thereafter, the first day to be counted is the day after the day on which the act, event or default occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to time periods that run from an occurrence (for example, death of a licensee triggering an application deadline); see Example 8 for illustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule—computation of terminal date
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided, when computing a period of time the last day of such period of time is included in the computation, and any action required must be taken on or before that day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by Example 9 showing how to count first and last days when a period is specified as X days after public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions applicable to computation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions for purposes of this section: 'holiday' means Saturday, Sunday, officially recognized Federal legal holidays and any other day on which the Commission's Headquarters are closed ...; 'business day' means all days ... which are not 'holidays'; 'filing period' means the number of days allowed ... for filing any document with the Commission; 'filing date' means the date upon which a document must be filed after all computations of time authorized by this section have been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains a Note enumerating Federal legal holidays (as of August 1987) and explains local variations (e.g., particular offices may be on holiday even if Headquarters is not). These definitions feed into how to count days and determine deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand-carried and electronic filing deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in §0.401(b), all petitions, pleadings, tariffs or other documents not required to be accompanied by a fee and which are hand-carried must be tendered for filing ... with the Office of the Secretary before 4 p.m. Documents filed electronically pursuant to §1.49(f) must be received by the Commission's electronic filing system before midnight. Applications, attachments and pleadings filed electronically in the Universal Licensing System (ULS) pursuant to §1.939(b) must be received before midnight on the filing date. Media Bureau applications and reports filed electronically pursuant to §73.3500 must be received by the electronic filing system before midnight on the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies different cutoff times for physical tendering vs. electronic filing and identifies the Secretary's role in determining pre-7:00 p.m. deadline compliance; compliance depends on the filing medium and cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate holidays when filing period is less than seven days
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided (e.g., §§1.773 and 76.1502(e)(1)), if the filing period is less than 7 days, intermediate holidays shall not be counted in determining the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 10 demonstrates excluding Saturdays and Sundays when counting a 5-day reply period; apply this rule before adding any mailing extensions per paragraph (h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing extension—additional three days for service by mail
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document is required to be served upon other parties by statute or Commission regulation and the document is in fact served by mail, and the filing period for a response is 10 days or less, an additional 3 days (excluding holidays) will be allowed to all parties in the proceeding for filing a response. This paragraph (h) shall not apply to documents filed pursuant to §1.89, §1.315(b) or §1.316. For purposes of this paragraph (h) service by facsimile or by electronic means shall be deemed equivalent to hand delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by Examples 11 and 12 showing how the 3-day mailing extension is added after computing the initial period (and excluding holidays from the added days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of computations when both short-period and mailing rules apply
rubrics_metrics.description: If both paragraphs (g) (short filing-period rule) and (h) (mailing extension) of this section are applicable, make the paragraph (g) computation before the paragraph (h) computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 13 demonstrates computing the short-period rule first (excluding intermediate holidays) and then adding the 3-day mailing extension to obtain the final deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: If filing date or Commission action falls on a holiday
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided, if, after making all the computations provided for in this section, the filing date falls on a holiday, the document shall be filed on the next business day. If a rule or order of the Commission specifies that the Commission must act by a certain date and that date falls on a holiday, the Commission action must be taken by the next business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 14 shows moving a filing date from Christmas Day to the next business day; applies equally to Commission action deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific provisions control over §1.4 general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where specific provisions of part 1 conflict with this section, those specific provisions of part 1 are controlling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites examples (e.g., §§1.45(d), 1.773(a)(3), 1.773(b)(2)) and warns practitioners to follow section-specific timing rules where they differ from the general §1.4 computations.
